row.why: For 'the customers were in a hurry / hectic' he used عجول - the Persian/MSA adjective (singular), a different lexical item that is not on her sheet; her word is مستعجل (sheet row 'in a hurry / rushed | Mista3jel | مستعجل'), plural مستعجلين. She let it pass and fixed only كنت راح تعمله in the clause before. Tier 1 not 2 because عجول is not a form of مستعجل; the singular-for-plural is a side effect of the wrong word, not the error.

row.amal_said: خرّبتي أو خرّبت. (36:48) No، خرّب، بـ-بخرب is the internal flipping. بخرّب is not.
row.why: For 'how many plans have you (f) ruined' he used the undoubled get-X pattern kharab/kharabit (خِرِب = it got ruined); she recast to خرّبتي أو خرّبت at 36:36, he asked again 'Isn't it kharabit?' (36:45) and she said No - بخرب is the internal-flipping one, بخرّب (doubled) is the make-X one; he then produced kharabti. D12 is the same slip and is folded in here.

row.medi_said: lama haket ziyada, ziyada ana, uh, kharab kul shee.
row.amal_said: [laughs] Some peo-- there's another term is like bakharrib ad-dunya.
row.right: أنا خرّبت كل شي (ana 5arrabt kul shi) - best reading
row.why: His own first clause is past ('lama haket ziyada' = when I said too much), so the second clause wants past 5arrabt: the bare 'kharab' after ana carries no person ending (B5) and no doubled middle (B12, the pattern she had just drilled). She did not fix the verb - she offered the idiom bakharrib ad-dunya / kharrabt ad-dunya. B1 (r2) would fit only if he meant a habit, but he chose a past verb for the first clause.
